meta.description: All professions for TDE4/DSA4.1 Basic Rules. Talent modifiers are cumulative with race and culture modifiers. Automatic advantages/disadvantages are included in gp_cost and must NOT be charged or refunded again. choice_blocks define mandatory choices the hero must make. Entries marked data_complete: false need verification from the PDF. Expanded to include additional professions and profession variants parsed from Wege der Helden; existing ids/values preserved where present.

professions.name: Messenger

talent_choice_modifiers.note: two trade languages from: Tulamidya, Rogolan, or Thorwalian, +4 each

professions.special_possession: proven horse with saddle and bridle
professions.description: Messengers are professional couriers who traverse all of Aventuria's roads and wilderness paths, delivering letters and packages. They are exceptional riders and navigators with broad geographic knowledge.

professions.name: Burglar
professions.special_possession: high-quality lockpicks (ease Lockpicking +3) and silk rope with silent grapple hook
professions.description: Burglars are professional thieves and infiltrators, masters of climbing, stealth, and lockpicking. They specialize in breaking into secured places and acquiring what others keep hidden.

professions.name: Explorer
professions.special_possession: mule with saddle OR small boat; tent; compass
professions.description: Explorers are adventurous scholars — geographers, historians, and scientists who venture into the unknown in search of knowledge. They have the broadest lore and language base of any profession.

professions.name: Mountebank

requirements.note: AG OR DE must be at least 13

professions.special_possession: donkey or mule loaded with one-person show equipment
professions.description: Mountebanks are wandering entertainers, jugglers, acrobats, and tricksters. Their exceptional body control and people skills make them among the most charismatic and physically agile heroes. They receive Dodge I and Sure-Footed free.

professions.name: Hunter
professions.special_possession: pack animal with equipment, or trained hunting dog / falcon
professions.description: Hunters are professional game hunters, trappers, and wilderness guides. They are the best at ranged combat, tracking, stealth, and wilderness survival. They receive Terrain Familiarity and the Sharpshooter SA free.

professions.name: Warrior
professions.special_possession: proven horse with saddle and bridle
professions.description: Warriors from the Havena military tradition are the most powerful fighters in the Basic Rules. They receive the highest combat talent bonuses, free Academic Training, Ambidextrous Combat I, Armor Familiarity I, and Shield Fighting I. The most expensive and demanding profession.

professions.name: Scout
professions.special_possession: trained horse and equipment, or donkey with expedition gear
professions.description: Scouts are military intelligence specialists and wilderness experts. They combine tracking, stealth, and mobility with moderate combat skills. They receive Terrain Familiarity and Local Knowledge free.

professions.name: Magician
professions.starting_spells_notes: Full list TBD — verify from BRW p. 78–80. Additional spells beyond Hauszauber listed above may exist.
professions.description: Guild Magicians are the only full human spellcasters in the Basic Rules. They have access to Guild Magic and General Spells. Their profession includes Academic Training and a significant ASP bonus. Metal armor interferes with spellcasting.
professions.data_notes: Full spell list and complete talent modifiers need verification from BRW p. 78–80.

professions.name: Pirate
professions.special_possession: chest with nautical/optical instruments (telescope, compass, quadrant)
professions.description: Pirates are sea raiders and sailors who live by boarding and plundering. They are cheap (1 GP), highly capable in maritime settings, and receive Sea Lore and Sure-Footed free. An automatic bad trait (Superstition or Greed) must be chosen.

professions.name: Knight

requirements.note: Traditionally male in most cultures; female Knights exist but are rare and culture-dependent

professions.special_possession: proven riding horse with saddle and bridle, lance
professions.description: Knights are noble warriors who have mastered mounted combat, jousting, and social graces. They receive Noble Birth free, along with Ambidextrous Combat I, Mounted Combat, Armor Use I, and Shield Fighting I. Noble obligations are mandatory.

professions.name: Mercenary
professions.special_possession: horse with saddle, or pack horse with tent and cooking gear
professions.description: Mercenaries are professional soldiers for hire. They have the most flexible weapon choice of any combat profession (+5 to one of six weapon categories). They receive Ambidextrous, Armor Familiarity I, and Shield Combat I free.

professions.name: Rogue

automatic_advantages.note: total SO value of 25, fences and informants

professions.special_possession: set of noble clothing and ornamental weapon; makeup kit
professions.description: Rogues are urban social manipulators — con artists, gamblers, informants, and charming criminals. They receive Social Chameleon and Connections free, making them the best social infiltrators in the Basic Rules.

professions.name: Physician
professions.special_possession: donkey with medical equipment; portable surgical kit
professions.description: Physicians are trained healers, surgeons, and herbalists. They have the best healing talent concentration of any profession and broad medical and botanical knowledge.
professions.data_notes: Talent modifiers partially reconstructed from context. Verify exact modifiers, GP cost, and attribute requirements from BRW p. 81.

professions.name: Legend Singer
professions.description: Legend Singers are elvish bard-mages who preserve and perform elvish lore through song and story. They combine magical abilities with exceptional performance and social skills.
professions.data_notes: Talent modifiers and GP cost TBD — encode from BRW p. 82. Elvish profession only.

professions.name: Ranger
professions.description: Rangers are elvish wilderness guardians — exceptional archers, trackers, and nature experts who also possess innate elvish magic. They are the most complete wilderness profession in the game.
professions.data_notes: Talent modifiers and GP cost TBD — encode from BRW p. 82. Elvish profession only.

professions.name: Al’Anfa
professions.description:
Overview:
Al’Anfa is a Wege der Helden profession or profession variant. It has been added to the expanded profession list using the same JSON shape as the existing records.

Training and role:
The profession should be interpreted through weapons, discipline, battlefield roles, armor, courage, and the social expectations of armed service. A hero with this profession has already spent part of life learning its methods, obligations, tools, jargon, and social expectations before becoming an adventurer.

Adventuring use:
Use the profession to decide what the character can plausibly know, who might recognize them, which authorities or guilds may claim them, what equipment feels natural, and which kinds of jobs or dangers they notice first.

Roleplaying notes:
Keep the background visible through habits, speech, contacts, old rivals, obligations, preferred gear, and the difference between professional pride and the compromises required by adventuring life.
